title: Plural 7: Prepositional (-ах / -ях)
description: The plural prepositional has one ending across all three genders: -ах after hard stems, -ях after soft stems. Always after a preposition: в, на, о / об, при.
descriptionRussian: Предложный падеж множественного числа: -ах после твёрдых основ и -ях после мягких. Всегда после предлогов в, на, о/об, при.
intro: The third and last of the easy cases, built exactly like the two before it. That is the regular plural complete: a nominative, an accusative that borrows, two hard lessons at the genitive, and three that share one shape. Compare it with the singular, where every case had its own gender split, and the plural starts to look like the language apologizing.
rules: The plural prepositional has one ending across all three genders. Hard stems take -ах; soft stems take -ях.
Hard stems (-ах): hard masc cons (журналах), hard fem -а (книгах), hard neuter -о (окнах), hushers (карандашах, врачах), velars (девочках, полках).
Soft stems (-ях): soft masc -й (музеях), soft masc -ь (учителях), soft fem -я (песнях), soft fem -ь (тетрадях), soft neuter -е (морях).
Family-plural masculines take -ьях: братьях, друзьях, сыновьях, стульях. Suppletive plurals: дети → детях, люди → людях.
Triggers: в + prep pl (location), на + prep pl (location, surface or idiomatic place), о / об + prep pl (about), при + prep pl (in the presence of, at the time of).
Spelling rule: о before a consonant-onset noun, об before a vowel-onset noun (об учителях, об окнах), обо in a few fixed phrases (обо мне, обо всех).
examples: Маша работает в больших офисах. (Masha works in large offices.) офис → офисах, hard masc + -ах.
Книги лежат на полках. (Books are lying on the shelves.) полка → полках, velar к + -ах.
Маша часто думает о друзьях. (Masha often thinks about her friends.) друг → друзьях, family-pl + -ьях.
Учитель рассказывает о книгах. (The teacher is talking about books.) книга → книгах, velar к + -ах.
Не говори при детях. (Don't say it in front of the children.) дети → детях, different-word plural + -ях.
Антон думает об учителях. (Anton is thinking about the teachers.) о → об before a vowel; учитель → учителях.

items.hint: Recap from L6: с + ? Hard fem -а pattern, instr pl ending?
items.explanation: L6 recap: с + instrumental for accompaniment. Коллега declines like fem -а; the instr pl is -ами: коллегами. Today's lesson moves to the prepositional plural, where the parallel form would be коллегах (after о, в, etc.).

items.hint: В + prepositional for static location. Офис is hard masc cons. The prep pl ending is?
items.explanation: В + prepositional plural for location. Офис is hard masc cons, so the prep pl is -ах: офисах. The same -ах ending appears on most hard stems, regardless of gender (журналах, книгах, окнах).

items.promptEnglish: There are many people on the streets.
items.hint: На + prepositional for location. Улица is hard fem -а. The prep pl ending is?
items.explanation: На + prepositional plural for surface or idiomatic places. Улица is hard fem -а, so the prep pl is -ах: улицах. Both в and на take the prepositional case, the choice between them is the same as in the singular (в for enclosed spaces, на for surfaces and events).

items.promptEnglish: Masha often talks about her friends.
items.hint: О takes the prepositional. Друг belongs to the -ья family. The prep pl ending is?
items.explanation: О + prepositional for the topic of speech / thought. Друг takes the family-plural pattern, so the prep pl is the irregular друзьях. Other family-pl masculines follow the same -ьях: братьях, сыновьях, стульях.

items.promptEnglish: The books are lying on the shelves.
items.hint: На + prepositional. Полка ends in velar к. The prep pl ending is?
items.explanation: На + prepositional plural for surface location. Полка is fem -а with velar к; the 7-letter rule blocks -ях (only relevant for soft stems anyway), and the spelling pattern is -ах: полках. Same logic as книгах, ручках, девочках.

items.promptEnglish: The teacher is talking about her daughters.
items.hint: О + prep pl. Дочь is 3rd-declension fem -ь with stem extension. The prep pl ending is?
items.explanation: Дочь is 3rd-decl feminine -ь and takes a stem extension in the plural (дочер- before the ending). The prep pl ending for soft stems is -ях: дочерях. The other stem-extension irregular is мать → матерях.

blanks: Дети учатся в хороших _____. (The children study in good schools.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: В + prepositional plural for location. Школа is hard fem -а, so the prep pl ending is -ах: школах.

errorCorrection.explanation: В for location takes the prepositional, and the prepositional plural of a hard masculine stem is -ах: в городах. Городамах is a double-ending blend of the dative -ам and the prepositional -ах and is not a real form. Each plural case has exactly one ending, so the prepositional is simply городах.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The teacher told us about distant seas.
errorCorrection.explanation: Море is a soft neuter noun (ending in -е), and soft stems take -ях in the prepositional plural: о морях. Морах wrongly applies the hard -ах ending. The preposition о forces the prepositional, and the soft stem supplies -ях, the same ending you saw in полях.

errorCorrection.sentence: Не говори об этом при детьми.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Don't talk about this in front of the children.
errorCorrection.explanation: При takes the prepositional, so дети uses the regular prepositional plural ending on its stem: при детях. Детьми is the special instrumental ('with the children', с детьми), pulled in here by sound-alike habit but wrong after при. The preposition fixes the case as prepositional, giving детях.

minimalPairs.explanation: О + prepositional for topic. Друг takes the family-pl ending in the prep pl: друзьях. Друзьям is the dative plural ('to friends'), which doesn't fit after о.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The books stand on the shelves.
minimalPairs.explanation: На + prepositional for surface location. Полка is hard fem -а; the prep pl is -ах by the spelling rule (velar к): полках. Полки is the plural nominative ('the shelves' as a subject), which doesn't fit after на.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each prepositional-plural phrase by the ending of the noun.

reviewVocab.definition: the prepositional plural; one ending across all three genders. Hard stems take -ах; soft stems take -ях. Always after a preposition.
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша живёт в больших городах' слово 'городах' стоит в предложном падеже множественного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: при + prepositional; flags a witness, audience, or temporal context. Common in 'не говори при детях' (don't say it in front of the children) and 'при царе' (in the time of the tsar).

the о / об / обо distinction; о before a consonant onset (о книгах), об before a vowel onset (об учителях, об окнах), обо in fixed phrases (обо мне, обо всех). The same rule applies in the plural as in the singular.
reviewVocab.example: Маша говорит о книгах, об учителях, обо всех своих друзьях.
